clue.text: Beg to be included among Jobcentre attendees

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the following words, included among their letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A claimant pleads to be counted among the people queuing at the Jobcentre.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is the UK government office where people sign on for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly or plead, a direct synonym of beg.

clue.text: Cut expenditure — on comedies possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A broadcaster trims its budget, perhaps by spending less on comedy shows.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to save money, so a past-tense verb meaning reduced spending.

clue.text: Article about yours truly making comeback? That's an idea!

blocks.note: the definite article
yours truly is the writer, that is me

explanation.surface: A writer pens a piece about their own return to the scene and thinks it a bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' only means concerning: the article is about me. The definition is the rest, a whimsical description of an idea that keeps returning.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a central idea, and in music or writing it is one that recurs, so it keeps coming back.

clue.text: Dear wife no longer brooding

blocks.note: a former wife is an ex
lost in sombre thought

explanation.surface: A man addresses his late or former wife, who no longer sits brooding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like a term of endearment for the wife, but it is the definition in its sense of costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced is a common synonym for costly or expensive.

clue.text: Acting companies on tour, did you say? Or soldiers?

indicators.note: asking whether you said something points to how a word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: touring theatre companies are troupes

explanation.surface: A puzzled listener wonders whether someone meant travelling actors or an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops is the plural word for soldiers, as in sending in the troops.

clue.text: Look to carry on in recession

indicators.note: recession means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: to keep on doing something is to carry on

explanation.surface: Advice to look ahead and keep going while the economy is in recession.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick look, so the noun is a brief glance.

clue.text: Little dog running up and down

indicators.note: a word that runs the same up the column as down it reads identically both ways

blocks.note: a young dog, whose three letters are the same in either direction

explanation.surface: A small dog dashes back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the word reads the same going up as going down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pup is a puppy, a young and therefore small dog.

clue.text: Eastern nation upset rival to boy at Harrow?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for east
taken as written

explanation.surface: An eastern country is upset by a rival of a Harrow schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton and Harrow are rival English boarding schools for boys; their annual cricket match is famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil of Eton College is the natural opponent of a pupil of Harrow School.

clue.text: I triumphed in broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word counts by sound

blocks.note: triumphed means won

explanation.surface: A contestant boasts of winning on a radio or TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker but is the Roman numeral for the number.
explanation.definitionFit: I is the Roman numeral standing for the number one.

clue.text: Scoff at bear repeatedly

blocks.note: Winnie-the-Pooh, the famous fictional bear
the bear's name said a second time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps mocking a bear, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh an idea is to dismiss it with contempt, an idiom for scoffing.

clue.text: Disappointed engineer trusted RAF

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A let-down mechanic who put faith in the Royal Air Force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a person but works as a verb. The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frustrated means thwarted and dissatisfied, close in sense to feeling let down.

clue.text: Poem about the cinema

blocks.note: a lyric poem
on means concerning, as in a talk on art

explanation.surface: Someone writes verse about going to the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The Odeon is a well-known chain of British cinemas, so a quick shorthand for the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is the name of a long-established British cinema chain, so it stands for a cinema.

clue.text: Bishop and I plugging nobleman's sparkling water

indicators.note: something plugging a hole sits inside it, so these letters go into the middle

blocks.note: a peer is a nobleman
Right Reverend, the title abbreviation used for a bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bishop and the speaker are sharing a lord's bottle of fizzy water.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop here is the Right Reverend, abbreviated as for a cleric's title. Perrier is a French brand of naturally sparkling mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Perrier is a well-known brand name of carbonated mineral water, so an example of sparkling water.

clue.text: One in charge of large tour abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A tour manager is responsible for a big trip overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tour abroad' reads as a holiday overseas, but 'abroad' is the signal to scramble both words.
explanation.definitionFit: A regulator is a body or official that controls and supervises something, so someone in charge.

clue.text: Broadcast by single politician causes damage

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Member of Parliament
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A lone politician's remarks on air do harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places the broadcast next to the single politician, so it comes after them.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or harm something, a verb synonym of damage.

clue.text: Soldier being discreet

blocks.note: first meaning: a soldier of the lowest rank
second meaning: kept to oneself, not public

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a tactful soldier; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is an army rank below corporal, and private also means confidential or secluded.

clue.text: A place to go for moles?

blocks.note: taken as written
the gents is the British name for a men's public toilet, a place one goes

explanation.surface: A question about where burrowing moles might head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moles' suggests the burrowing animal, but here they are spies planted inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a spy embedded in an organisation, so moles are secret agents.

clue.text: Look back at satirical show on radio

indicators.note: on radio things are only heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a revue is a light theatrical entertainment of sketches, often satirical

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a satire programme broadcast on the wireless.
explanation.definitionFit: To review is to go over or reconsider past events, so to look back at them.

clue.text: Curse I heard after returning as it happens

indicators.note: returning means coming back the way it went, so the word is written backwards
heard tells us to take the sound of the word, not its spelling

blocks.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens
the letter's name is said the same as the organ of sight

explanation.surface: Someone says they caught a curse on the way back, as it happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the sound of I behind the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent glance believed to put a curse on its target.

clue.text: Some exile murdering a Madagascan native

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the answer is a portion of the next words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A grim tale of an exile killing a native of Madagascar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' reads as a person, but the definition is an animal found only on Madagascar.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are primates found in the wild only on Madagascar, so they are native to that island.

clue.text: Detective Inspector, horny creature having change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart swaps out the central letter for a different one

blocks.note: a moose has large antlers, so it is horny

explanation.surface: A police inspector is likened to an antlered beast that has had a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle O of the animal is replaced by R. Inspector Morse is the Oxford detective of Colin Dexter's novels and the TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is the surname of the fictional Detective Inspector created by Colin Dexter.

clue.text: Obese top celebrities: one accepting of his lot?

blocks.note: obese means fat
the A-list is the most famous tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Overweight stars, and someone who just shrugs and accepts things.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatalist believes events are predetermined and so resigns himself to whatever fate brings.

clue.text: Girl losing her head, the idiot

indicators.note: losing a head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl panics and someone calls her a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Lass is a Scottish and northern English word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish person, a common synonym for an idiot.

clue.text: Turning tail, sailor is a traitor

indicators.note: turning tail means turning round to go back, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: tar, short for tarpaulin, is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor who runs away is branded a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for someone who deserts or betrays their side, like a rat leaving a ship.

clue.text: What cat does in street

blocks.note: first meaning: a cat's cry, as a verb
second meaning: a narrow street of converted stables

explanation.walkthrough: A mews is a British back lane of former stables, now often homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat mews when it cries, and a mews is a type of small British residential street.

clue.text: Backing inexperienced leader, an explosive sort

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the next word is read in reverse

blocks.note: a raw recruit is inexperienced
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Supporting a green leader with a fiery temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Explosive sort' sounds like a hot-tempered person, but the definition is a weapon part.
explanation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive payload at the front of a missile, a kind of explosive device.
